title: Burg Laudegg Ladis
highlights: Spectacular castle fortress dominating a mighty slate rock terrace above the castle pond
Romanesque square keep constructed in the early 13th century
Iconic postcard motif gracing the sunny Serfaus-Fiss-Ladis plateau
Historically pivotal administrative seat for the Upper Court region
kurzbeschreibung: Burg Laudegg perches on a sheer slate cliff above the castle pond in Ladis, defining the iconic panorama of the sun terrace.
beschreibung:
Romanesque Fortress above the Castle Pond

Burg Laudegg ranks among Tirol's most striking castle complexes. Built upon a sheer slate rock pinnacle high above the village of Ladis at 1,176 metres above sea level, together with the reflecting castle pond at its foot, it forms a world-famous postcard motif.

Historic Seat of Power

First recorded in documents in 1239, Burg Laudegg served for centuries as the administrative seat of the Oberes Gericht court. Its sturdy square keep and the walls of the palas have been meticulously restored over recent decades, giving the historic village scape of Ladis its unmistakable and romantic character.
